name: Laos
summary_text: Laos demands real caution from trans visitors. Nothing criminalises being trans, and Laos has a socially visible tradition of trans feminine people; but there is no legal gender recognition, no anti-discrimination protection, no registered LGBT organisation (the one-party state restricts all civil society), and no documented recourse. Vientiane and Luang Prabang are accustomed to tourists; the risk is administrative (an opaque state) more than violent.

sources.title: Laws and Policies Analytics | Joint Analysis | Lao People's Democratic Republic
sources.claim_summary: UNAIDS Laws and Policies analytics page for the Lao PDR filtered to transgender-related laws and policies - a database interface showing legal instruments affecting trans people in Laos (no criminalisation of same-sex conduct; limited specific protections).
ADB publication on the legal status of sexual and gender minorities in Asia and the Pacific - regional comparative overview covering Laos among other countries.

sources.title: A History of LGBT Criminalisation | Human Dignity Trust
sources.claim_summary: Human Dignity Trust: 'A History of LGBT Criminalisation' - almost 500 years of outlawing LGBT people; overview of jurisdictions that criminalise and strategic litigation worldwide (Laos context: no current criminalisation but no protections).

sources.title: Gay Laos: Lost and Found 2000
sources.claim_summary: GlobalGayz 'Gay Laos: Lost and Found' (2000/2009): Richard Ammon's account of a small Vientiane lesbigay circle - restaurants, friendships, romantic relationships; a picture of quiet, low-key gay life in communist Laos.

sources.title: Overcoming a government crackdown on social media in Laos | Science and Technology | Al Jazeera
sources.claim_summary: Al Jazeera (Oct 2018): 'Overcoming a government crackdown on social media in Laos' - 'net idols' face retribution for online posts; 'You can't post anything about the government' - the free-expression climate that constrains LGBT visibility.

sources.title: EU celebrated IDAHO Day in Vientiane | EEAS
sources.claim_summary: EU External Action Service: the EU celebrated IDAHO day (International Day Against Homophobia) in Vientiane - diplomatic visibility for LGBT rights in Laos (page largely navigation content at fetch time).
